current_episode.title: How To Build Sustainable Growth And Profitability In A Creative Business - Winning with Kass Laboucane and Michelle Scully, Co-Founders of Spark and Pony

guest.bio_context: Cass Laboucane is a writer by trade who co-founded Spark and Pony Creative with Michelle Scully after both worked together in a marketing department. She recently became a new mother and has been instrumental in building the agency's messaging and content strategy over seven years while learning to delegate and empower team members.

context.real_quote: A lot of conventional business advice is always telling you to grow, grow, push your team harder. And in the last 12 months we've been redefining success as stability.

Four years: period during which Cass and Michelle operated as a two-person partnership before hiring team members
17 years: Michelle Scully's experience in the branding and marketing industry
Nine months: age of Cass Laboucane's baby at time of interview
Last 12 months: timeframe during which the founders redefined success from growth to stability
58,000 views and 625 hours of watch time on YouTube: metrics for Executive Wins Podcast
2,800 audio downloads: number of downloads on Apple Podcasts and Spotify for the podcast

pending_qa.q: How does mentorship accelerate learning for creative business founders?
pending_qa.r: Cass and Michelle work with mentor Ben Burns, who owns an agency in the United States and runs an accelerator program for the creative industry globally. They acknowledged they should have sought mentorship earlier and that having an outside voice you trust in your industry who has actually succeeded helps provide feedback and prevents making every mistake the hardest way.

pending_qa.q: What happens when a creative agency consolidates its service offerings?
pending_qa.r: Michelle described cutting a bunch of service offerings as feeling like a weight coming off her shoulders, allowing the team to finally let go of some things and focus on the work they absolutely love and do really well. Consolidating services makes processes more repeatable and easier for team members to learn and take over internally.

pending_qa.q: How can one email marketing channel unexpectedly unlock revenue for a business?
pending_qa.r: During a brand consultation, Michelle suggested a client reactivate their email marketing, which they had neglected. After the consultation, the client powered that channel back up and subsequently sold out of all their product, demonstrating how a simple strategic gap identified during consulting can produce immediate revenue results.
